meaning: after the impossible-goal record (met false, failed true) the goal is ENDED, not held: the next bare /goal prints the fixed words 'No goal set. Usage: `/goal <condition>`' and a /goal clear prints the fixed words 'No goal set'; no goal_status record of any kind is written for either, and the failed record itself was written about 13 seconds after the set sentinel in the measured run
not_a_clear: no sentinel with met true was written for the /goal clear, so a give-up never reads as a clear
run: claude -p, haiku, four turns joined by --resume: an unreachable goal, a bare /goal, /goal clear, then a second goal

meaning: a goal set after a give-up writes the ordinary set sentinel (met false, sentinel true) and a second Goal set: line, then runs to its own met true verdict; no record links it to the given-up goal, so 'replaced' cannot be read from the later goal alone
